stimulus.text: Paraphrase of standard accounts of three sisters agriculture: maize, beans, and squash were planted together in the same field. Tall maize stalks held climbing bean vines. Broad squash leaves spread across the ground below, shading the soil. Together the three crops fed dense, settled populations in eastern North America.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of standard accounts; see grounding.

stem: The 'three sisters' system, interplanting maize, beans, and squash in the same field, sustained dense Native populations in eastern North America. Which statement best explains why this system could support large, settled communities?

options.text: It required iron plows and teams of draft animals to work the soil.
It succeeded only in desert regions where very little rainfall occurred.
It was designed to grow surplus crops for export to European markets.
It produced three food crops from one cleared field, raising each field's yield.

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
